source: no published source and no manual; read from the installed 2.0.0 plugin.dylib and its res/Logic.svg

lines: Four two-input logic gates, all performing the same operation, which is chosen from the right-click menu
One of the two inputs to the topmost gate, counted high above 1.2V and low at or below it; with nothing patched it reads 0V, which is low
The other input to the topmost gate, counted high above 1.2V and low at or below it; with nothing patched it reads 0V, which is low
The A input of that gate, counted high above 1.2V and low at or below it; with nothing patched it takes the voltage from the A jack of the gate above, and from the one above that if it is empty too
The B input of that gate, counted high above 1.2V and low at or below it; with nothing patched it takes the voltage from the B jack of the gate above, and from the one above that if it is empty too
The result of the chosen operation on that gate's two inputs, 10V when the result is true and 0V when it is false
Note — all four gates perform one operation together, and there is nothing on the panel that sets it: the choice is on the right-click menu, and a new module comes up as AND
Note — the lamps across the top show which of the six operations is chosen, and each gate has a lamp for each of its two inputs and one for its output; none of them can be clicked
Note — the table printed in the middle of the panel gives the result of all six operations for each of the four combinations of two inputs
Note — leaving a gate's jacks empty and feeding only the topmost gate sends the same pair of signals down all four gates, which is what the normalling is for
Menu — Logic Operation: AND, NAND, OR, XOR, NOR, XNOR — sets the operation all four gates perform

Logic.notes: The module declares no parameters at all, so the operation can only be changed from the context menu; a reader who does not open it has a module that is permanently an AND gate. The panel prints A, B and OUT beside every gate with no number on any of them, while the maker's tooltips number them 1A, 1B, 2A and so on; the lines follow the panel and describe the one jack that was clicked. The high threshold is 1.2V rather than the 1V a Rack Schmitt trigger uses, and it is compared as a level every sample rather than as an edge, which is right for a logic gate. The normalling chain is the module's one hidden feature and nothing on the panel shows it: an unpatched A or B jack reads the same letter from the gate above, walking up until it finds a patched one or reaches the top, where it reads 0V. The plugin ships no source and no manual; everything above was read out of the compiled binary, whose symbols are intact. Menu item names were recovered as inlined string immediates in LogicWidget::appendContextMenu: 0x4e41 with 0x44 for AND, 0x414e with 0x444e for NAND, 0x524f for OR, and so on, under the label "Logic Operation".
